article.title: NFL EDGE Friday Morning Brief
article.dek: The Browns beat the Steelers 27-24 on Thursday night, the morning board moves the Hit Rate card to the Bills, and Justin Jefferson's Friday practice is the day's big tell.

items.headline: Cleveland takes Thursday night, 27-24
paragraphs: Thursday night is final: the Browns beat the Steelers 27-24 in Cleveland. Andre Szmyt hit a 56-yard field goal with 10 seconds left, and Grant Delpit intercepted Aaron Rodgers' last throw to seal it. Deshaun Watson threw for 268 yards and a touchdown with one interception; Rodgers threw for 299 yards and three touchdowns but was picked twice, and the Browns sacked him five times.
Cleveland is 3-1 and alone in first place in the AFC North. Pittsburgh is 2-2. The division logjam broke on the first game of the week.
items.takeaway: Week 4's first result is a Browns win — the AFC North looks different than it did yesterday.

items.headline: The injury news, all in one place
paragraphs: Justin Jefferson missed practice again Thursday — two straight days with the ankle sprain. The Vikings call him day-to-day, the scans showed nothing long-term, and Kevin O'Connell says they won't rush him back until he looks like himself. Today's practice is the tell. Final designations land this afternoon, and the Dolphins are in Minnesota on Sunday at 4:05 p.m. ET.

The Bears still have not named a Week 4 starter. Ben Johnson was non-committal Wednesday and pointed out that Tyson Bagent ended training camp as the No. 2. Caleb Williams is still out with the hamstring. Case Keenum was the star Monday night (247 yards, two passing touchdowns, one rushing score) and the app still projects him — but that's a projection, not an announcement. If Johnson names Bagent today, the board won't know yet, and that's exactly what Check is for: type in your book's Bears line and get a bet-or-no-bet verdict on YOUR price.

Elsewhere from yesterday's reporting: Puka Nacua is expected to play Sunday for the Rams, Nico Collins is on track for Houston, and Mike Evans missed Thursday's practice for Tampa Bay. Today's designations settle all of it.
items.takeaway: Today's question marks get answered today — check back this afternoon for designations.

items.headline: Weather: nothing to price this morning
paragraphs: No NFL games today, so there is no kickoff-window weather to check. Sunday's outdoor games get their final forecasts in tomorrow's editions, and that's when weather earns its paragraph.
items.takeaway: Sunday's weather check lands tomorrow — today is about the injury designations.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: The Hit Rate card moved — the Bills are the new read
paragraphs: Hit Rate is the card that answers one question: which supported pick looks most likely to win. It forgoes value for win probability — the app's own tutorial says Hit Rate is not Profit Rate. This morning the answer changed. Yesterday evening the card read Bears moneyline at -175 on DraftKings. The morning board reads Bills moneyline at -298 on DraftKings instead.

The numbers on the new read: the app gives Buffalo a 71.2% chance to win, MEDIUM reliability, at a price of -298. Price mechanics: -298 means every $2.98 you risk wins $1. The evaluator's expected value is slightly negative, and that's fine — this card is not chasing +EV, it's chasing the win. The card follows the price, and Buffalo's win probability is higher than what Chicago was showing, so the card moved.
items.takeaway: The card follows the price — the most-likely-to-win read is now the Bills.

items.headline: Balanced and Value agree: Bears -3.5 at -104
paragraphs: Balanced is the middle ground — a strong pick without paying too much, a good starting point for a new bettor. Value is always the +EV read. This morning both cards are reading the same number: Bears -3.5 at -104 on FanDuel. The app's fair price is -105, so FanDuel is dealing three cents better than fair. Model cover chance: 50.5%, MEDIUM reliability, +2.19% expected value. Price mechanics: -104 means every $1.04 you risk wins $1.

When two different cards land on one number, that's the number the board is asking about. Your stake comes from the app — it sets it from your bankroll and its deliberately conservative staking, so you don't guess. And when you're ready, the app logs the ticket: it only tracks what you actually enter, winners and losers both.
items.takeaway: Two cards, one question: is Bears -3.5 at your book's price worth it?

items.headline: The Bears number moved two cents against the card — and the card held
paragraphs: Bears -3.5 on FanDuel went from -102 yesterday evening to -104 this morning. Two cents against the reader. The evaluator's expected value slipped from +3.2% to +2.19%, but the card did not flinch — it's still a BET, and -104 is still inside the card's play-through of -3.5 at -107. The card reads prices, not teams: when the number it needs disappears, it goes looking for a new one. This one didn't disappear.

Bills moneyline drifted from -290 to -298 on DraftKings overnight, eight cents of drift, and the Hit Rate card followed the price to Buffalo. The Bills spread held steady all night: -7 at -105 on DraftKings, -6.5 at -122 on FanDuel. The Patriots +6.5 at even money from earlier in the week is gone and it's not coming back.

The board refreshes every morning and evening. If your book shows a different number than the board on any of these — a different spread, a different price — don't guess. Tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and the evaluator for a bet-or-no-bet verdict on YOUR price. A full re-evaluation, not a blind override.
items.takeaway: The moves are in the board. Bet your book's number, not the board's.

items.headline: Same games, different prices — shop the number
paragraphs: The books don't agree with each other this morning, and that's the whole game. Bills moneyline: -298 on DraftKings, -340 on FanDuel — the same win costs you 42 cents more at FanDuel. Patriots-Bills spread: -7 at -105 on DraftKings vs -6.5 at -122 on FanDuel. Rams-Eagles: -3.5 on both DK and FanDuel, but Pinnacle deals -3.0 at -131 — a full key number cheaper, though you pay extra juice for it.

None of these disagreements change what the cards read. They change what YOU pay. When the books disagree on the number, the board's read only applies to the price the board priced — your ticket lives or dies on your book's number. That's the Check pitch again, and it never gets old.
items.takeaway: Your book's price is the only price that matters for your ticket.

items.headline: Friday is decision day
paragraphs: Today is the day the question marks resolve. Final practice reports and injury designations land this afternoon: Justin Jefferson's ankle, the Bears' quarterback, and the rest of the watch list. Then on Sunday, inactive lists drop about 90 minutes before each kickoff — that's when the last game-time calls get made.
This morning's brief can't have any of that. What it can do is tell you what to watch: check back this afternoon for designations, and Sunday morning for inactives.
items.takeaway: Check back this afternoon — the injury picture sharpens on Friday.

items.headline: Betting term of the day: steam move
paragraphs: A steam move is a sudden line shift when a wave of respected money hits one side at several books in a short window. Example from this week: the Bills went from -6.5 to -7 on DraftKings on Thursday afternoon — the market re-pricing, not one book guessing.
A steam move is a price alert, not a pick. It tells you where the money went, not who's right. And sometimes, like this morning, it just moves the card off a price that no longer exists.
items.takeaway: Steam = the price moved fast. It doesn't tell you which side to take.
